summary: AI Agent Question Capture — API Key Auth + Spring AI MCP Tool Integration
description:
Supporters currently compile interview questions in an external AI chat (e.g. claude.ai, perplexity.ai) and re-enter each one manually via <backend/api/src/main/java/xyz/catuns/imp/api/question/QuestionController.java>. This epic lets an MCP-capable AI client (Claude.ai remote connector, Claude Desktop) call the backend directly during a live interview to look up context (clients, candidates, sessions, existing questions) and create + link new questions to the active session in one turn, authenticated via a supporter-issued API key rather than a JWT.

Design decisions this epic implements:
- New `ROLE_AI_AGENT` Spring Security authority, distinct from the human `UserRole` enum — attached only to API-key authenticated requests, never to a user's own JWT.
- The key is issued by and tied to an owning supporter, but ROLE_AI_AGENT reads are global (any client/session/candidate), not scoped to the issuing supporter's own assignments — resolved explicitly in this conversation's planning after considering a narrower `questions:read/write`-only scope.
- ROLE_AI_AGENT write access is limited to question creation and session-question linking — no feedback, status transitions, or user/client mutation, regardless of what the issuing supporter's own JWT role could do.
- Bulk question creation is reframed as a session operation, not a standalone question-bank operation: `POST /sessions/{sessionId}/questions/bulk` creates and links a list of questions to a session in one call, using the same per-item partial-success pattern already established in <backend/api/src/main/java/xyz/catuns/imp/api/scheduleimport/ScheduleImportService.java> (`ImportRowResult`/`ImportSummaryResponse`) — one bad item does not roll back the rest of the batch.
- MCP tools are thin in-process adapters over the existing service layer (no internal HTTP hop), so `@PreAuthorize` enforcement is identical whether the caller reached the operation via REST or via an MCP tool call.
- Destructive/out-of-scope operations (delete, unlink, status transitions, feedback, user/client writes) are deliberately excluded from both the agent's REST grants and its MCP tool surface.
userType: Interview supporter using an external AI chat (Claude.ai / MCP-capable client) during a live interview
functionality: let their AI assistant look up client, candidate, and session context and create + link interview questions directly to the active session from within the chat, without manually re-entering each question through the dashboard afterward
benefit: questions surfaced conversationally during the interview are captured immediately and accurately at the source, eliminating manual post-interview transcription and reducing the chance a question is forgotten or mis-recorded

stories.summary: Add ApiKey entity and self-service issuance endpoints
stories.description:
New `apikey` module (<backend/api/src/main/java/xyz/catuns/imp/api/apikey>) mirroring the existing module layout (entity/, dto/, repository/, service + controller at package root, matching <backend/api/src/main/java/xyz/catuns/imp/api/question>). Adds an `ApiKey` entity, Flyway migration, repository, issuance service, and controller exposing `POST /api-keys`, `GET /api-keys`, `DELETE /api-keys/{id}`.

Raw key format: `aik_` + base62(32 random bytes). Only a `keyPrefix` (first 12 chars, plaintext, for identification in the UI) and a SHA-256 `keyHash` (unique indexed, used for O(1) lookup on every request) are persisted — chosen over BCrypt because the raw key already carries 256 bits of entropy, so slow salted hashing buys nothing and would prevent an indexed lookup. The full raw key is returned exactly once, in the create response, and is never stored or retrievable again. Default `expiresAt` is now + 90 days, capped at a 180-day maximum enforced by request validation.

Entity shape:
```
ApiKey
  id            UUID
  ownerId       UUID        -- FK users.id, indexed
  name          String      -- supporter-chosen label
  keyPrefix     String(12)  -- plaintext, shown in UI
  keyHash       String(64)  -- SHA-256 hex, unique indexed
  scope         enum        -- AI_AGENT (single value for now)
  revoked       boolean     -- default false
  revokedAt     Instant     -- nullable
  expiresAt     Instant
  lastUsedAt    Instant     -- nullable
  createdAt     Instant
```

acceptanceCriteria.then: a 201 response is returned containing the raw key exactly once, plus id/name/keyPrefix/expiresAt; the persisted ApiKey row contains only keyHash and keyPrefix, never the raw key

acceptanceCriteria.given: a supporter with 2 previously issued keys
acceptanceCriteria.then: both keys are returned with keyPrefix, lastUsedAt, expiresAt, and revoked status — no hash or raw key field is present in the response

acceptanceCriteria.given: an active key owned by the caller
acceptanceCriteria.then: the key is soft-revoked (revoked=true, revokedAt set), the endpoint returns 204, and subsequent authentication attempts with that key are rejected

acceptanceCriteria.given: an ADMIN caller and a key owned by a different supporter
acceptanceCriteria.then: the revoke succeeds — owner-or-admin authorization, so a leaked key can be killed even if the owning supporter is unavailable

stories.summary: Authenticate API-key requests and introduce ROLE_AI_AGENT
stories.description:
Add an `ApiKeyAuthFilter` that validates the `X-API-Key` header (deliberately not `Authorization`, so it can't collide with the JWT Bearer scheme already handled by the `jwt-spring-boot-starter`) against `ApiKeyRepository.findByKeyHash`, and populates a Spring Security `Authentication` — principal resolves to the key's owning supporter, single granted authority `ROLE_AI_AGENT` — for valid, non-revoked, non-expired keys.

<backend/api/src/main/java/xyz/catuns/imp/api/config/SecurityConfig.java> does not currently define a `SecurityFilterChain` bean — it is supplied entirely by the external `jwt-spring-boot-starter` autoconfiguration, whose source isn't visible from this repo. The first task is a short spike to determine the correct extension point before the filter is wired in.

Once authentication works, widen `@PreAuthorize` on the specific existing service methods the agent needs: unrestricted reads on clients/sessions/questions (not scoped to the issuing supporter, per the decision that agent lookups are global), and write access on question creation/linking — explicitly not inheriting the `isAssignedSupporter` restriction that applies to the human SUPPORTER role on <backend/api/src/main/java/xyz/catuns/imp/api/question/SessionQuestionService.java>.

acceptanceCriteria.when: a request includes header X-API-Key: <raw key>
acceptanceCriteria.then: the request proceeds with an Authentication whose sole authority is ROLE_AI_AGENT and whose principal resolves to the key's owner; ApiKey.lastUsedAt is updated
the request is rejected with 401 before reaching any controller

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Agent reads are not scoped to the issuing supporter
acceptanceCriteria.given: a key issued by Supporter A
acceptanceCriteria.when: the caller requests a session assigned to Supporter B via the sessions read endpoints
acceptanceCriteria.then: the session is returned — agent reads are global, per the decision that lookups aren't row-scoped to the issuing supporter

acceptanceCriteria.when: the caller attempts a feedback, status-transition, or user/client mutation endpoint
acceptanceCriteria.then: the request is rejected with 403 — ROLE_AI_AGENT was never granted on those methods

stories.summary: Extend session-question linking to accept a batch, applied directly to the session
stories.description:
Add `POST /sessions/{sessionId}/questions/bulk` accepting a `CreateSessionQuestionRequest { List<CreateSessionQuestionItem> questions }`, where each item carries the <backend/api/src/main/java/xyz/catuns/imp/api/question/dto/CreateQuestionRequest.java> fields plus the optional displayOrder/notes fields from <backend/api/src/main/java/xyz/catuns/imp/api/question/dto/LinkQuestionRequest.java>.

Each item creates a Question and links it via SessionQuestion in its own `@Transactional(propagation = REQUIRES_NEW)` unit of work, following the exact per-row partial-success pattern already used in <backend/api/src/main/java/xyz/catuns/imp/api/scheduleimport/ScheduleImportService.java> (ImportRowResult / ImportSummaryResponse) — one bad item (invalid clientId, failed validation) does not roll back the rest of the batch. This replaces the current two-step create-then-link flow for the bulk case, and is the endpoint both the REST/API-key path and the MCP `add_questions_to_session` tool call into.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a session and 5 well-formed question items
acceptanceCriteria.then: 201 is returned with 5 CREATED outcomes, each including the new questionId and sessionQuestionId

acceptanceCriteria.given: a batch of 5 items where item 3 has an unknown clientId
acceptanceCriteria.then: items 1, 2, 4, and 5 are created and linked; item 3's result reports FAILED with an error reason; the response still reflects the successful items rather than aborting the whole batch

acceptanceCriteria.given: a human SUPPORTER (JWT) calling this endpoint for a session not assigned to them
acceptanceCriteria.then: 403 is returned, per the existing isAssignedSupporter restriction on SessionQuestionService — this endpoint does not loosen human-caller authorization, only the new ROLE_AI_AGENT path is unscoped

stories.summary: Add name-searchable user lookup endpoint for candidate/supporter resolution
stories.description: <backend/api/src/main/java/xyz/catuns/imp/api/user/UserController.java>'s existing GET /users is admin-only and has no free-text name filter, so it can't back a "find the candidate named Sarah" tool call from a non-admin agent key. Add `GET /users/lookup?query=&role=` returning a minimal `UserLookupResponse { id, name, role }` — deliberately excluding email/active/other fields to keep the agent-facing surface low-exposure. Open to ADMIN, SUPPORTER, MARKETER, and the new AI_AGENT authority.

acceptanceCriteria.then: 200 is returned with a result containing id, name "Sarah Connor", and role CANDIDATE — no email or other fields present

acceptanceCriteria.when: the endpoint is called with just a query string
acceptanceCriteria.then: results span all roles matching the name query

stories.summary: Expose question-capture operations as MCP tools via Spring AI MCP Server
stories.description:
Add the Spring AI MCP Server starter and mount an MCP server (SSE endpoint, e.g. /mcp/sse) secured by the same ApiKeyAuthFilter/ROLE_AI_AGENT path established in the authentication story. Implement 8 @Tool-annotated methods across two beans:

- LookupTools (read-only): search_clients, search_candidates, search_sessions, get_session, search_questions, list_session_questions
- QuestionWriteTools (write): add_questions_to_session, link_existing_question

Each tool is a thin adapter calling the existing service layer in-process (no internal HTTP hop), so @PreAuthorize enforcement is identical to the REST path. This is the mechanism a Claude.ai remote MCP connector or Claude Desktop uses to call the backend live from a chat. Delete/unlink, question update, status transitions, feedback, and user/client mutation are deliberately excluded from the tool surface.

acceptanceCriteria.then: 401 is returned, consistent with the REST API-key path
